title: Agent platform entry
description: What one agent platform provides, category by category, with the evidence that shows an agent uses it and the vendor documentation each claim comes from. One file per platform in data/agent-platforms/platforms/. tools/ci/check-agent-platforms.mjs validates every file against this schema.

id.description: Lower-case id, the same as the file name without .json.

vendor.description: The company or project behind the platform.

name.description: The platform as this entry groups it, for example 'LangGraph and LangSmith'.

summary.description: One or two neutral sentences on what the entry covers.

products.description: The products this entry groups, because they work as one.

documentation.description: URL prefixes where the vendor's own documentation lives. Every source URL in this file starts with one of them.

tracing.title: Tracing and telemetry
tracing.description: Recording what an agent did (model calls, tool calls, steps, tokens, latency) and sending it somewhere it can be viewed. Open standard: OpenTelemetry, including its generative AI semantic conventions.

evaluations.title: Evaluations
evaluations.description: Scoring an agent's outputs or runs against datasets, rubrics, graders or human review, offline or on live traffic.

prompt-management.title: Prompt management
prompt-management.description: Storing, versioning and fetching prompts outside the agent's code.

keys-and-secrets.title: Keys and secrets
keys-and-secrets.description: Where the agent's API keys and credentials for other systems are kept and how the agent reads them at run time.

memory-and-state.title: Memory and saved state
memory-and-state.description: Saving a run's state (checkpoints, threads, sessions) so it can resume, and memory that lasts across runs.

human-approval.title: Human approval steps
human-approval.description: Pausing a run for a person to approve, edit or answer, and resuming it afterwards.

deployment.title: Deployment and scaling
deployment.description: Where and how the agent is run as a service, and how it scales.

sandboxes.title: Sandboxes and code execution
sandboxes.description: Running code the agent writes, or giving the agent a computer, browser or file system, in an isolated environment.

tool-connections.title: Tool connections (MCP support)
tool-connections.description: How the agent connects to tools and other systems. Open standard: Model Context Protocol (MCP). The rating says whether MCP is supported.

agent-to-agent.title: Agent-to-agent (A2A support)
agent-to-agent.description: How the agent calls, or is called by, agents running elsewhere. Open standard: Agent2Agent (A2A). The rating says whether A2A is supported. Several agents inside one program is not this category.

identity-and-access.title: Identity and access
identity-and-access.description: Who the agent is, how it signs in to other systems, and who may call it or change it. Open standards: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.

packaging.title: Packaging (Agent Plugins 1.0.0, Agent Skills)
packaging.description: The form an agent or its parts travel in. Open standards: Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (https://agent-plugins.org) and Agent Skills (https://agentskills.io). The rating says whether these are supported.

name.description: The product as the vendor names it.

kind.description: framework: a library the agent's code imports. hosted-service: a service the vendor runs. low-code: agents made in the vendor's designer rather than in code.

license.description: An SPDX license id for open source, or 'proprietary'.

rating.description: native: the platform's own feature. standard: provided through an open standard. partial: only part of the category is covered. none: the documentation says the platform does not provide it. unknown: not found in the documentation.

what.description: A short factual sentence naming the feature as the vendor names it.

level.description: open-standard: the data or interface follows an open standard. open-source: the vendor's own interface, open source, runs anywhere. proprietary: the vendor's own interface, only from the vendor. mixed: parts of more than one, said in the note. not-applicable: for a none rating. unknown: not found.

standards.description: Open standards the feature uses or offers a path through.

note.description: Whether the data or interface follows an open standard, and any standard-based path the vendor offers.

evidence.description: What an inspector looks for in an agent's code to tell whether the agent uses this feature.

sources.description: The vendor's own documentation the claims come from.

kind.description: package: a dependency name in a manifest (pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, package.json, .csproj, pom.xml). import: an import or using line. call: a function, class, method or decorator in code. env: an environment variable name. file: a file name or path. config: a key inside a config file. cli: a command in scripts, a Dockerfile or CI. not-in-code: the feature is set up outside the agent's code, so the code shows nothing; the note says where it is set.

value.description: The literal text to search for.

openness.description: How open the part of the feature this item shows is, when that differs from the cell's portability level (a mixed cell's open part and its vendor's own part). open-standard: the part follows an open standard, named in `standard`. open-source: the vendor's own interface, open source, runs anywhere. proprietary: the vendor's own interface, only from the vendor. Left out, the item takes the cell's level.

standard.description: The open standard this item's part follows, one of the cell's portability.standards. Only with openness open-standard.
